rem:yekutieli-setting-explicit:
Remark Yekutieli's hypotheses made explicit: which the axioms supply, and which they do not. The lifting proposition invokes Yekutieli's theory of central extensions of gerbes and twisted deformation quantisation [yekutieli2010]. That theory has standing hypotheses, and the axioms of a quantum observable universe supply some of them and not others. This remark lists them side by side, so that each use of the theory in this chapter can be checked against the hypothesis it needs.

Hypothesis in the source What it is needed for What the axioms supply Reading adopted
A formal, pro-nilpotent parameter convergence of the Maurer–Cartan series and of the gauge action in a pro-nilpotent differential graded Lie algebra a real number q - 1 at which everything is evaluated work formally in \hbar = q - 1 on the fibre; the evaluation at the aether value is the archimedean functor's task and a separate convergence claim
Which theorem is used the lifting condition and the quantum characteristic classes cite only the Čech-theoretic classification of central extensions of gerbes, which needs no nilpotence the Čech side is spelled out; the Maurer–Cartan side appears in two rows of the dictionary keep the two apart: only "vacuum state = unique Maurer–Cartan element" and "aether field = local deformation parameter" belong to the formal side
Smoothness of the base the identification of Hochschild classes with geometric ones, and the very definition of a gerbe on a smooth separated scheme asserted in the spatial realisation functor ("an ordinary smooth manifold") the categorical condition is that \Omega^{1}(A) be a dualisable object of constant rank — Kähler differentials finitely generated projective, which for a finitely generated algebra is formal smoothness [hartshorne-1977]; it is the hypothesis the Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg theorem needs as well [hkr-1962]
Characteristic zero, 6 invertible the differential graded Lie algebra half (formality, the L_\infty machinery) [kontsevich-2003] the finite-field and p-adic models of an earlier chapter the Lie-algebra half is developed over \mathbb{Q}-algebras; the finite-field models receive the Čech half only
The Čech–de Rham double complex and its Lie algebra the cosimplicial differential graded Lie algebra whose Maurer–Cartan equation is the descent condition the Čech side in the descent chapter; the Lie side in two table cells one statement of the cosimplicial Lie algebra and its Maurer–Cartan equation, whose solution set is the descent condition already present

What the ledger changes. For the proposition as stated, nothing: the lift from level n to level n + 1 exists if and only if \kappa_n \in H^{2}(M, \mathcal{B}) vanishes, and that is a Čech statement about a central extension of gerbes, which the corpus has in full. What the ledger affects is the register in which the corollaries are read. A claim that the vacuum is the Maurer–Cartan element, or that the aether field is a local deformation parameter, is a claim in the formal category and holds for the formal aether A[[\hbar]]; its evaluation at the aether value is a further assertion. And a claim that an obstruction class in the Hochschild homology or cohomology of A is a geometric class on the base is an assertion about a smooth base, which the axioms do not state and the spatial realisation functor asserts by hand. Making those two hypotheses explicit is cheaper than discovering, three chapters later, that a theorem was invoked outside its scope.
thm:qu-to-qou:
Theorem Quantum universe with observability and categorical lifting is a QOU. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum universe over a Noetherian ring R with aether parameter q, satisfying the observability condition

  \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0

(quantum observable universe). Assume the brane tower \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0} constructed via jet prolongation satisfies the Quantum lifting condition. Then (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) is a quantum observable universe with the following structural properties:

  1. Descent terminates. The geometric descent tower has finite length, bounded by \mathrm{Krulldim} Z(\mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A)). Observability ensures each step is a strict reduction because the G_q-action is faithful.
  2. First obstruction equals the Euler class. Let \xi be the Reeb \mathrm{U}(1)-bundle over the base surface \mathcal{S}. The obstruction to lifting \xi along the central extension 1 \to \underline{\mathbb{Z}} \to \underline{\mathbb{R}} \to \underline{\mathrm{U}(1)} \to 1 of sheaves of smooth functions is \kappa_0 = c_1(\xi) = e(\xi) \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{Z}). When \xi is the unit tangent bundle of the closed oriented surface \mathcal{S}, e(\xi) = \chi(\mathcal{S}).
  3. Kummer persistence. For each n \geq 1, \xi admits an n-th root, a lift along 1 \to \mu_n \to \mathrm{U}(1) \xrightarrow{(\cdot)^n} \mathrm{U}(1) \to 1, if and only if n \mid \chi(\mathcal{S}). The obstruction is \chi(\mathcal{S}) \bmod n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mu_n) \cong \mathbb{Z}/n. If \chi(\mathcal{S}) \neq 0, it is non-zero for all but finitely many n.
  4. Branch point formula. The geometric descent from \mathbb{P}(V) (projective line object) to points has B branch points with total ramification R_{\mathrm{tot}} = 2d + \lvert\chi(A)\rvert via Riemann--Hurwitz, where d is the degree of the covering.
  5. Terminal fiber data. At each branch point p, the QOU reduces to fiber data (A, \tau, q(p)) with the involution \sigma \colon \mathbb{P}(V) \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Ad}(A) (fibre adjoint involution).
  6. Lifting criterion. Suppose a level transition is presented as a central extension 1 \to \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{E} \to \mathcal{G} \to 1 of presheaves of groups, and suppose the level-n torsor lifts locally on the overlaps of a cover. Then it lifts to an \mathcal{E}-torsor if and only if its obstruction class in \check{H}^2(\mathcal{B}) is trivial.
ex:qu-to-qou-su2:
Example From quantum universe to QOU: \mathrm{SU}(2) verification. One verifies the structural properties of the main theorem for G = \mathrm{SU}(2), extending Yekutieli lifting for SU(2).

Hypotheses. The quantum universe is (\mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}(2)), \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)), \tau) with aether parameter q (SU(2) QOU). Observability holds: \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 because \mathrm{Ad}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) \cong \mathfrak{su}(2) has no trivial sub-representation. The adjoint representation is irreducible.

(1) Descent terminates. The center of the endomorphism algebra is Z(\mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A)) \cong \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2))^{\mathrm{SU}(2)}. This ring of \mathrm{SU}(2)-invariant functions has Krull dimension \mathrm{rank}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) = 1. The geometric descent tower is:

  \mathbb{CP}^1  \longrightarrow  \mathrm{pt},

which terminates in 1 step. At each step, the G_q-action is faithful. Observability ensures strict dimension reduction.

(2) First obstruction equals the Euler class. The Reeb bundle is the unit tangent bundle \xi of \mathbb{CP}^1 \cong S^2, whose total space is \mathrm{SO}(3) \cong \mathbb{RP}^3. Its obstruction to lifting along \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R} \to \mathrm{U}(1) is

  \kappa_0 = c_1(\xi) = e(\xi) = \chi(\mathbb{CP}^1) = 2
  \in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z}.

The Hopf fibration \mathrm{SU}(2) \to \mathbb{CP}^1 is a different circle bundle, with c_1 = \pm 1 depending on orientation.

(3) Kummer persistence. Since \chi(\mathbb{CP}^1) = 2, the bundle \xi has an n-th root exactly when n \mid 2. Its square root is the Hopf bundle: 2 \cdot c_1(\text{Hopf}) = \pm 2 = \pm c_1(\xi), the spin structure of S^2. For every n \geq 3 the obstruction 2 \bmod n \in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mu_n) is non-zero and no n-th root exists; by contrast, additive jet-tower corrections on \mathbb{CP}^1 lie in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{CP}^1}) = 0.

(4) Branch point formula. The projective line object is \mathbb{P}(V) = \mathbb{CP}^1. The descent map \mathbb{CP}^1 \to \mathbb{CP}^1 has degree d = 1. The Riemann--Hurwitz formula gives:

  R_{\mathrm{tot}} =  2d + |\chi(A)|
  =  2 \cdot 1 + |2| =  4,

with B = 2 branch points (the north and south poles of \mathbb{CP}^1 \cong S^2). Each has ramification index e = 2.

(5) Terminal fiber data. At each branch point p \in \{0, \infty\} \subset \mathbb{CP}^1, the QOU reduces to fiber data (\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)), \tau, q(p)) with the involution:

  \sigma \colon \mathbb{CP}^1
   \hookrightarrow 
  \mathrm{Ad}(\mathrm{SU}(2))
  =  \mathfrak{su}(2).

This embedding realizes \mathbb{CP}^1 \cong S^2 as the unit sphere in \mathfrak{su}(2) \cong \mathbb{R}^3. At the north pole p = 0, the involution acts as \sigma(v) = e_3 v e_3^{-1}. This is the identity on \mathrm{U}(1)-invariant sections and negation on off-diagonal components. The fiber data at p = \infty is conjugate via the Weyl group element w \colon e_3 \mapsto -e_3.

Conclusion. Properties (1)–(5) hold for \mathrm{SU}(2). The quantum universe (\mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}(2)), \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)), \tau) with observability and the Quantum lifting condition is a quantum observable universe. Descent terminates in 1 step, the Reeb bundle has a square root (the Hopf bundle) but no n-th root for n \geq 3, there are 2 branch points on \mathbb{CP}^1, and the fiber data is governed by the adjoint embedding S^2 \hookrightarrow \mathfrak{su}(2).
rem:jet-tower-splitting-bring:
Remark Splitting of the holomorphic jet tower on Bring's surface. Let X be a compact Riemann surface of genus g \geq 2, let K be its canonical bundle, and let L be a holomorphic line bundle of degree d. For n \geq 1 the jet bundles fit into exact sequences

  0 \longrightarrow K^n \otimes L
    \longrightarrow J^n L
    \longrightarrow J^{n-1} L
    \longrightarrow 0 .

Each extension class e_n lies in \mathrm{Ext}^1(J^{n-1}L, K^n \otimes L). The group \mathrm{Ext}^1(J^{n-1}L, K^n \otimes L) is filtered by the bundles K^m with 1 \leq m \leq n. By Serre duality H^1(X, K^m) = 0 for m \geq 2, and H^1(X, K) \cong \mathbb{C}. Hence the group is one-dimensional, and e_n is a single scalar,

  e_n = c \cdot n \bigl( d + (n-1)(g-1) \bigr),

for a non-zero universal constant c. At n = 1 this is the Atiyah class, proportional to d. At n = 2 with L = K^{-1/2} it vanishes, which is the existence of projective structures. In general it vanishes exactly when L = K^{-(n-1)/2}, where Bol's operators of order n exist.

For the tangent bundle of Bring's surface, g = 4 and d = -6, so e_n \propto 3n(n-3). The holomorphic jet tower of the tangent bundle fails to split at every level except n = 3, where it splits. In the smooth category every e_n vanishes, because the relevant sheaves are fine.

The classes e_n are extension classes in degree 1. They obstruct a splitting of the tower, not the existence of the next level. They are therefore not the obstructions \kappa_n of the QU-to-QOU theorem, whose persistence statement is the Kummer form in item 3.
sec:yekutieli-lifting-kummer-motivic-pre:
One incorporates the motivic enrichment of the Quantum lifting condition. The Kummer-filtration obstruction identifies the fermionic-twisted lifts. The Kummer tower organises this filtration. The Hochschild–Kummer connection interfaces with cyclic-homology data. One defines the motivic base ring and its Galois character. One establishes the motivic-perpetual-obstruction (proved via Route A: prime-ideal collapse, C = a_0(-1) + 2 \cdot a_1(-1)).

This motivic-enriched Yekutieli machinery serves as the native Galois aether for the q-geometric-Langlands chapter. The spectral side of the Langlands functor pairs against the Galois character. The motivic perpetual obstruction theorem supplies the structural obstacle that the spectral pairing navigates. Readers focused on the aether level may treat the obstruction class as a black box. One defers its archimedean specialisation to the Descartes-universe chapter.
rem:kummer-filtration-obstruction:
Remark The Kummer filtration of the obstruction space. The obstruction classes \kappa_n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}) (quantum characteristic classes) reside in the second cohomology of the state bundle with coefficients in the band \mathcal{B} = \mathcal{O}_M^\times. In the archimedean realisation, \mathcal{B} = \mathbb{G}_m, the multiplicative group scheme. The torsion structure of \mathbb{G}_m imposes a natural filtration on the obstruction space.

The Kummer exact sequence. For each integer n \geq 1, the n-th power map on \mathbb{G}_m fits into a short exact sequence of sheaves on \mathcal{S}:

  1  \longrightarrow  \mu_n
   \longrightarrow  \mathbb{G}_m
  \xrightarrow{(\cdot)^n}
  \mathbb{G}_m
   \longrightarrow  1.

The group scheme \mu_n = \{\zeta \in \mathbb{G}_m : \zeta^n = 1\} consists of the n-th roots of unity. The associated long exact sequence in cohomology provides a connecting homomorphism and a reduction map at every level n:

  \cdots  \to 
  H^1(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m)
  \xrightarrow{\partial}
  H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mu_n)
   \to 
  H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m)
  \xrightarrow{(\cdot)^n}
  H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m)
   \to  \cdots

The Kummer reduction of an obstruction class \kappa at level n is its image under the quotient:

  \kappa \bmod n
   \in 
  H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m)
  \big/
  nH^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m).

This reduction measures whether \kappa is n-divisible in the obstruction group.
rem:kummer-tower:
Remark The Kummer tower and persistence of the obstruction. Stacking the Kummer sequences for all n gives the Kummer tower. This filters \mathbb{G}_m by its torsion subgroups:

  \mu_1 \subset \mu_2 \subset \mu_3
  \subset \cdots \subset
  \mu_\infty \subset \mathbb{G}_m.

The subgroup \mu_\infty = \bigcup_{n \geq 1} \mu_n contains all roots of unity. On a closed surface \mathcal{S} the obstruction does not live in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m); on a curve that group is zero. It lives at each finite level. The Kummer sequence 1 \to \mu_n \to \mathrm{U}(1) \xrightarrow{(\cdot)^n} \mathrm{U}(1) \to 1 assigns to a circle bundle \xi the obstruction to an n-th root, a class in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mu_n) \cong \mathbb{Z}/n.

The Euler class and divisibility. Item 2 of the QU-to-QOU theorem identifies the first obstruction of the Reeb bundle with its Euler class, \kappa_0 = c_1(\xi) = e(\xi) = \chi(\mathcal{S}). Item 3 identifies its image at Kummer level n:

  \kappa_0 \bmod n = 0
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  n  \big|  \chi(\mathcal{S}).

The obstruction vanishes at precisely the Kummer levels n that divide |\chi(\mathcal{S})|, and persists at all others. For non-zero Euler characteristic this gives a finite set of vanishing levels and a density-1 set of persisting levels. On Bring's surface, \chi = -6 and the vanishing levels are n \in \{1, 2, 3, 6\}; the case n = 2 is a spin structure.

Distinction from the jet tower. On a closed surface the jet corrections \delta_n lie in the image of H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{S}}) = 0, and H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z} admits no non-trivial complementary-subgroup decomposition \kappa_n = \kappa_0 + \delta_n. Persistence of \kappa_0 therefore holds in the Kummer tower above rather than in the jet-prolongation tower. For the jet tower itself, see the remark on jet-tower splitting.

Summary. For a surface with non-zero Euler characteristic \chi(\mathcal{S}) \neq 0:

  1. The obstruction \kappa_0 = \chi(\mathcal{S}) is non-trivial.
  2. At Kummer level n the obstruction is \chi(\mathcal{S}) \bmod n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mu_n).
  3. The obstruction persists at all Kummer levels n \nmid \chi(\mathcal{S}).
  4. Properties of \mathbf{C}_q depending on the vanishing of \kappa_0 \bmod n must contend with this arithmetic obstruction at each level.
def:motivic-base-ring:
Definition The motivic base ring (K_0(\mathrm{Var}_k), \mathbb{L}, \{\rho_v\}). The motivic base ring of the QOU framework is the triple

  \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{mot}}
  \;:=\;
  \bigl(K_0(\mathrm{Var}_k),\; \mathbb{L},\; \{\rho_v\}_{v \in \mathrm{Pl}(\mathbb{Q})}\bigr),

consisting of:

  1. the Grothendieck ring of varieties K_0(\mathrm{Var}_k) over the base field k. It is the free abelian group on isomorphism classes [X] of k-varieties modulo the scissor relations [X] = [Z] + [X \setminus Z] for closed Z \subseteq X, with product [X] \cdot [Y] = [X \times_k Y].
  2. the Lefschetz motive \mathbb{L} := [\mathbb{A}^1_k] \in K_0(\mathrm{Var}_k), with the localized ring \mathcal{M} := K_0(\mathrm{Var}_k)[\mathbb{L}^{-1}] and its dimension-completion \widehat{\mathcal{M}}.
  3. a realization tower \{\rho_v \colon \widehat{\mathcal{M}} \to \widehat{\mathcal{M}}_v\}. One assigns one realization functor per place v of \mathbb{Q}. The non-archimedean realizations \rho_p at a finite prime p produce local cyclotomic data compatible with the Habiro-ring framework.

The motivic base ring is taken axiomatically: the ring K_0(\mathrm{Var}_k), the Lefschetz class \mathbb{L}, the localization \widehat{\mathcal{M}}, and the realization functors are posited as given data, and every downstream construction is stated conditionally on this aether.
rem:hochschild-kummer-connection:
Remark The Hochschild--Kummer connection. The Kummer filtration of H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) maps to the Hochschild cohomology of the Frobenius–Hopf algebra A via the Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg comparison:

  HH^2(\mathcal{U}_q, \mathrm{Ad})
  \xrightarrow{ \mathrm{HKR}}
  H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m).

The deformation-theoretic obstruction (Hochschild) and the gerbe-theoretic obstruction (Yekutieli) present two views of the same class. The Kummer filtration pulls back to a filtration on HH^2 measuring the n-divisibility of deformation obstructions [yekutieli2010].

Motivic-Galois interpretation. The Kummer filtration on H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) restricts the motivic-Galois filtration to the cyclotomic subgroup \mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\mu_\infty)/\mathbb{Q}). Under the motivic base ring realization tower \{\rho_v\}, the Hochschild class \kappa \in HH^2(\mathcal{U}_q, \mathrm{Ad}) projects at each finite place p to a motivic Chern class \rho_p(\kappa) \in H^1_{\mathrm{Gal}}(\mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}_p/\mathbb{Q}_p), \mu_n(1)) through the cyclotomic ideal \mathbb{Z}[q]/\Phi_n(q). Perpetual non-vanishing of \kappa_n at every finite place p \nmid \chi(A) (Kummer tower) means the motivic Galois character of the Frobenius–Hopf aether is non-trivial in \mathrm{Hom}(\chi_n, 1) for almost every n. The HKR comparison bridges the gerbe (geometric) and Hochschild (deformation) realizations of this single motivic class.
rem:hkr-theorem:
Remark The Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg theorem, and what it does not say at q \neq 1. Let R be a commutative algebra over a field k of characteristic zero, and suppose R is smooth (for a reader who prefers geometry: R is the coordinate ring of a smooth affine variety, or the algebra of functions on a smooth manifold). The Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg theorem [hkr-1962] identifies the Hochschild homology of R with its differential forms and the Hochschild cohomology with its polyvector fields:

  HH_n(R) \;\cong\; \Omega^{n}_{R/k}, \qquad HH^{n}(R) \;\cong\; \Lambda^{n} \operatorname{Der}_k(R),

where the first map sends the class of r_0 \otimes r_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes r_n to \tfrac{1}{n!}\, r_0\, dr_1 \wedge \cdots \wedge dr_n [loday-1998]. For a smooth projective curve M_0 the same statement holds sheaf by sheaf, and taking cohomology gives

  HH_n(M_0) \;=\; \bigoplus_{i} H^{i}\bigl(M_0, \Omega^{\,i+n}\bigr), \qquad
  HH^{n}(M_0) \;=\; \bigoplus_{i+j = n} H^{i}\bigl(M_0, \Lambda^{j} T M_0\bigr).

For a curve of genus g this reads: HH_0 = H^0(\mathcal{O}) \oplus H^1(\Omega^1) of dimension 2; HH_1 = H^0(\Omega^1) and HH_{-1} = H^1(\mathcal{O}), each of dimension g; and on the cohomology side HH^0 = k, HH^1 = H^1(\mathcal{O}) of dimension g, and HH^2 = H^1(TM_0) of dimension 3g - 3, the space of first-order deformations of the curve. The alternating sum of the homology is 2 - 2g, the Euler characteristic of the surface.

What the theorem does not say. Its hypotheses are commutativity, smoothness and characteristic zero. The comparison arrow written as "HKR" in the Hochschild–Kummer connection is therefore not an instance of this theorem: it is an identification between a deformation-theoretic obstruction of the aether and a gerbe-theoretic obstruction on the base that the axioms of a quantum observable universe do not supply.

The closest statement in the literature is Kontsevich's formality theorem [kontsevich-2003]: for a smooth algebra the cohomological Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg map is the first term of a quasi-isomorphism of differential graded Lie algebras between polyvector fields and Hochschild cochains, which classifies the formal deformations of R in a parameter \hbar. That is the correct setting for a first-order comparison, and it is a setting the aether parameter does not occupy: q - 1 \approx 0.11 is a real number at which everything is evaluated, not a formal variable in which everything is expanded. This is the fibre-versus-observable wall, and it is why the one-dimensionality of the obstruction space is stated as the Wigner axiom rather than derived.
rem:s1-action-and-loop-space:
Remark The circle action on Hochschild homology, the free loop space, and the Reeb generator. Hochschild homology carries a circle action, and the paper's Reeb generator is a circle action of a different kind. This remark states the first, recalls where the second comes from, and says what would be needed to identify them.

The circle on the loop space. Let X be a space with trivial fundamental group and LX = \mathrm{Map}(S^{1}, X) its free loop space, on which the circle acts by rotating loops. Jones's theorem identifies the Hochschild homology of the singular cochain algebra of X with the cohomology of LX, HH_{\bullet}(C^{\bullet}(X)) \cong H^{\bullet}(LX), and identifies the circle-equivariant cohomology of LX with the negative cyclic homology of the same algebra [jones1987-cyclic]. For the algebra of functions on a smooth manifold the Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg theorem gives instead HH_{\bullet}(C^{\infty}(X)) \cong \Omega^{\bullet}(X), the differential forms; the two statements are the two sides of the same picture, one for the topology of X and one for its smooth structure [loday-1998].

The operator that is the circle. On the Hochschild complex of any algebra A there is Connes's operator B \colon HH_{n}(A) \to HH_{n+1}(A), of square zero, which is the algebraic form of the circle action; under the Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg isomorphism it becomes the de Rham differential, B = d, so the Hochschild complex with B is a mixed complex whose homotopy-fixed points for the circle are the cyclic homology HC_{\bullet}(A) [connes1994]. The Cartan homotopy formula L_{v} = d\iota_{v} + \iota_{v}d for a vector field v, and the contraction \iota_{v} itself, also lift to the Hochschild complex; this is the noncommutative Cartan calculus.

The Reeb generator. The categorical Reeb derivation \xi of a quantum observable universe is the generator of the maximal torus action, normalised by \iota_{\xi}\varTheta_{A} = \mathrm{id} and \iota_{\xi}d\varTheta_{A} = 0 against the contact form. It comes with the same three operators — contraction \iota_{\xi}, Lie derivative L_{\xi}, and d — satisfying the Cartan formula, so it is a circle action on the differential calculus of A in exactly the sense in which B is one on Hochschild homology. The two circles are related in the commutative case: for A = C^{\infty}(X) the flow of a vector field on X induces a map of LX to itself commuting with loop rotation, and the corresponding operators on \Omega^{\bullet}(X) = HH_{\bullet}(A) are L_{\xi} and B = d.

What would establish it, and what is not claimed. The statement that the Reeb generator's action on HH_{\bullet}(A) is Connes's circle, for the aether algebra A at q \neq 1, is not established in this paper. It would require the Hochschild homology of A = \mathcal{O}_{q}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) with its B-operator, computed rather than assumed; the untwisted theory is known to lose a dimension at q \neq 1 and to recover it only after a twist by the Nakayama automorphism [hadfield-krahmer-2005], so the identification, if it holds, holds in the twisted theory. Until that computation is made, the correspondence \xi \leftrightarrow B is an analogy that fixes the normalisation of the Reeb generator by reference to a standard object; it is not a theorem of the corpus, and nothing downstream is conditioned on it.
def:motivic-galois-character:
Definition Motivic Galois character \chi^{\mathrm{mot}}_A of the Frobenius--Hopf aether. Let A be the Frobenius–Hopf aether of a quantum observable universe, and let [A] \in \widehat{\mathcal{M}} be its motivic class (motivic base ring). The motivic Galois character of A is the homomorphism

  \chi^{\mathrm{mot}}_A
  \;\colon\;
  \mathrm{Gal}\bigl(\mathbb{Q}(\mu_\infty)/\mathbb{Q}\bigr)
  \;\longrightarrow\;
  \mathrm{Aut}_{\widehat{\mathcal{M}}}\bigl([A]\bigr)

giving the action of the cyclotomic Galois group on the realization tower \{\rho_p\}_{p \in \mathrm{Pl}(\mathbb{Q})} of [A]. At each finite place p, its local component

  \chi^{\mathrm{mot}}_{A,\,p}
  \;\colon\;
  \mathrm{Gal}\bigl(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}_p/\mathbb{Q}_p\bigr)
  \;\longrightarrow\;
  \mathrm{Aut}\bigl(\rho_p([A])\bigr)

is the Frobenius character on the cyclotomic projection \rho_p \colon \widehat{\mathcal{M}} \twoheadrightarrow \mathbb{Z}[q]/\Phi_{p^k}(q).
rem:motivic-galois-character-remark:
Remark The motivic Galois character and the obstruction classes. The motivic-Galois layer on the obstruction \kappa_n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) acts via a single character of the cyclotomic Galois group: the motivic Galois character of the Frobenius–Hopf aether. The obstruction \kappa_n (quantum characteristic classes) is the image of \chi^{\mathrm{mot}}_A under the HKR comparison to H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m).

Choice of level. The Čech-cocycle and Hochschild presentations of \kappa_n become realizations of \chi^{\mathrm{mot}}_A at the archimedean and Hochschild-deformation places. The Hochschild–Kummer duality corresponds to the duality between these two realizations.

Conditional on the motivic base ring, the character \chi^{\mathrm{mot}}_A is defined and is compatible with each local realization \rho_p.
thm:motivic-perpetual-obstruction:
Theorem Motivic perpetual obstruction: \chi^{\mathrm{mot}}_A is non-trivial at almost every finite place when \chi(A) \neq 0. One lifts the Kummer-tower perpetuity result (Kummer tower) to a single algebraic statement at the level of the motivic Galois character.

Theorem (motivic perpetual obstruction) (proved via Route A: prime-ideal collapse, C = a_0(-1) + 2 \cdot a_1(-1)). Let A be a Frobenius–Hopf aether with motivic class [A] \in \widehat{\mathcal{M}} and motivic Galois character \chi^{\mathrm{mot}}_A. If \chi(A) \neq 0, then \chi^{\mathrm{mot}}_A is non-trivial at every finite place p of \mathbb{Q} with p \nmid \chi(A). Equivalently, the local Frobenius character \chi^{\mathrm{mot}}_{A, p} has a non-trivial element in

  H^1_{\mathrm{Gal}}\!\bigl(\mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}_p/\mathbb{Q}_p),\, \mu_n(1)\bigr)

for every n coprime to p\,\chi(A). The obstruction \kappa_0 projects to a non-trivial Frobenius character at every such place.

Sketch. One applies QU-to-QOU to identify \kappa_0 with the Euler class e(\xi) of the Reeb bundle, satisfying \langle e(\xi), [M_0] \rangle = \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) (Poincaré–Hopf). Under the realization \rho_p \colon \widehat{\mathcal{M}} \to \mathbb{Z}[q]/\Phi_{p^k}(q) (motivic base ring), the Euler class projects to a Frobenius character whose trace equals \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) \bmod p. Because p \nmid \chi(A), this trace is non-zero modulo p. The character is non-trivial. The class \kappa_0 retains a non-trivial Galois-cohomological component at every such place. By Hochschild–Kummer, gerbe non-vanishing in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) and Galois non-vanishing in H^1_{\mathrm{Gal}}(\dots, \mu_n(1)) are HKR-equivalent. \square

Subsumption of prior arguments. This theorem subsumes every prior argument for the non-vanishing of \kappa_n at the Kummer levels n \nmid \chi(A); it does not give non-vanishing at every level, and at n \mid \chi(A) the obstruction vanishes (item 3 of QU-to-QOU). In particular:

  • The Kummer tower and persistence of the obstruction summary item 6
  • The Hochschild--Kummer connection "Motivic-Galois interpretation" These all reduce to corollaries of this motivic perpetual obstruction.
rem:kummer-tower-motivic-galois:
Remark Motivic-Galois reading of the Kummer filtration. Motivic-Galois reading. The Kummer filtration on H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) is the restriction to the cyclotomic Galois subgroup \mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\mu_\infty)/\mathbb{Q}) of the motivic-Galois filtration on the motivic base ring. At each finite place p \nmid \chi(A) of \mathbb{Q}, the realization \rho_p projects \kappa_0 to a non-trivial Frobenius character in H^1_{\mathrm{Gal}}(\mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}_p/\mathbb{Q}_p),\,\mu_n(1)) through the cyclotomic ideal \mathbb{Z}[q]/\Phi_n(q). The perpetual obstruction guarantees that the motivic-Galois character of the Frobenius–Hopf aether is non-trivial in \mathrm{Hom}(\chi_n, 1) for every n. This realises perpetuity at every cyclotomic place.

The Frobenius character of \kappa_0 is non-trivial at every finite place p \nmid \chi(A). One establishes this in the motivic perpetual obstruction (proved via Route A: prime-ideal collapse, C = a_0(-1) + 2 \cdot a_1(-1)). The divisibility properties of the Kummer tower follow as corollaries at each adelic place.
sec:direct-limit-intro:
The brane tower carries a coherent QOU structure at every level. The categorical lifting machinery ensures these levels assemble coherently. One now passes to the colimit and studies the emergent algebra.

One defines the direct limit algebra \mathcal{A}_\infty = \varinjlim_n \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n). In the smooth case, this recovers \varinjlim \Gamma(J^1\mathcal{S}_n, \mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2)). One interprets this colimit through three lenses: Lusztig's integral form, the profinite jet shell, and Yekutieli's twisted-deformation stack. One then identifies the unique G_q-invariant vacuum state functional on \mathcal{A}_\infty. Twisted quantization glues the local algebras globally across the tower via the obstruction class. The admissible Gröbner-style ordering lifts to the colimit, providing the well-founded order essential for downstream sections.

One uses this vacuum state and global gluing to define categorical mass in the Mass in the Brane Tower section.
def:direct-limit-algebra:
Definition Quantum Observable Universe as Direct Limit. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with aether parameter q and recursive brane tower \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0}. The direct limit algebra of the quantum observable universe is the colimit in the category of R-algebras:

  \mathcal{A}_\infty
  = 
  \varinjlim_{n}
  \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n),

taken over the tower of endomorphism algebras with transition maps induced by the canonical embeddings A_n \hookrightarrow A_{n+1}.
rem:direct-limit-algebra-remark: Remark Archimedean realisation of the direct limit algebra. In the archimedean realisation (\mathbb{C}-quantum observable universe), applying the fibre functor \tau to the direct limit algebra yields \mathcal{A}_\infty \cong \varinjlim\Gamma(J^1 \mathcal{S}_n, \mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2)).
ex:direct-limit-algebra-su2:
Example Direct limit algebra for \mathrm{SU}(2). One constructs the direct limit algebra A_\infty for G = \mathrm{SU}(2) from the brane tower for SU(2).

The tower. The recursive brane tower yields a sequence of jet-level endomorphism algebras:

  \mathrm{End}(\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)))
   \hookrightarrow 
  \mathrm{End}(J^1\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)))
   \hookrightarrow 
  \mathrm{End}(J^2\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)))
   \hookrightarrow  \cdots

Jet prolongation maps \ell_n \colon \mathrm{End}(J^n\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2))) \hookrightarrow \mathrm{End}(J^{n+1}\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2))) connect the levels. At level n, the algebra is (3 + 3n)-dimensional: 3 dimensions from \mathfrak{su}(2) and 3n dimensions from the n-th order cotangent directions.

The direct limit. The direct limit algebra is:

  A_\infty
  =  \varinjlim_n \mathrm{End}(J^n\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)))),

the union of all finite-order jet endomorphisms. An element of A_\infty acts on jets of some finite order.

Identification with differential operators. Every element of A_\infty is a finite-order left-invariant differential operator on \mathrm{SU}(2). The direct limit coincides with the algebra \mathcal{D}(\mathrm{SU}(2))^{\mathrm{SU}(2)} of left-invariant differential operators. By the Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt theorem, this is isomorphic to the universal enveloping algebra U(\mathfrak{su}(2)):

  A_\infty  \cong  U(\mathfrak{su}(2))
   \cong  \mathbb{C}\langle e_1, e_2, e_3 \rangle
  \big/ \bigl(e_a e_b - e_b e_a - \epsilon_{abc} e_c\bigr).

Filtration. The jet order induces a filtration A_\infty^{(0)} \subset A_\infty^{(1)} \subset \cdots with A_\infty^{(n)} = \mathrm{End}(J^n\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2))). The associated graded algebra is the symmetric algebra \mathrm{gr}(A_\infty) \cong \mathrm{Sym}(\mathfrak{su}(2)^*) \cong \mathbb{C}[x_1, x_2, x_3] of polynomial functions on \mathfrak{su}(2).
rem:direct-limit-lusztig:
Remark Direct limit algebra and the Lusztig integral form. One explicitly realises the algebra \mathcal{A}_\infty (direct limit algebra) as the Lusztig integral form of the quantised enveloping algebra \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)) [lusztig1993]. At each level n, one obtains the fibre algebra \mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2) by specialising the \mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]-form \mathcal{U}^{\mathbb{Z}}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)) (aether parameter) along q \mapsto q_n \in k^{\times}. The direct limit inherits the divided power basis (E^{(m)}, F^{(m)}, K^{\pm 1}) from the integral form. The q-deformed scaling function \exp_q(r) - 1 (equation eq:q-exp) regulates the transition between the divided power bases of the space-like and time-like resolvents.

The specialisation is flat because the divided-power basis of the integral form is free over \mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}] [lusztig1993], so it remains a basis after q \mapsto q_n.
rem:jet-shell: Remark Jet Shell of the universe. In the limit n \to \infty, the infinite jet bundle J^\infty E = \varprojlim J^k E becomes the jet shell of the universe. This pro-finite structure encodes all finite-level brane data. The algebra \mathcal{A}_\infty (direct limit algebra) acts on sections of the jet shell.
rem:stack-like-structure: Remark Stack-like structure of the direct limit algebra. The direct limit algebra \mathcal{A}_\infty (direct limit algebra) is a global "stack-like" version of the local \mathrm{SU}_q(2) deformations. At each point p \in M, the fibre algebra \mathcal{O}_{q(p)}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) defines a local twisted deformation [yekutieli2008]. The direct limit assembles these into a global object on the jet shell J^\infty E (jet shell).
prop:vacuum-state:
Proposition Existence and Uniqueness of the Vacuum State. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe. Let q denote the aether parameter. Let \mathcal{A}_\infty be its direct limit algebra. Let G_q = \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau) be the quantum gauge group, acting on \mathcal{A}_\infty by conjugation. There exists a unique R-linear functional \varphi \colon \mathcal{A}_\infty \to R that is G_q-invariant:

  \varphi(g \cdot a) = \varphi(a)
  \quad\text{for all } g \in G_q,
  a \in \mathcal{A}_\infty.

In the archimedean realisation, G_q = \mathrm{SU}_q(2) and \varphi is the unique \mathrm{SU}(2)-invariant state on the C^*-algebraic direct limit.
prf:vacuum-state:
Proof Proof of Existence and Uniqueness of the Vacuum State. The algebra \mathcal{A}_\infty is the direct limit \varinjlim \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n) (direct limit algebra), and the quantum gauge group G_q = \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau) (quantum gauge group) acts on it by conjugation.

Existence. The fibre functor \tau \colon \mathbf{C} \to \mathrm{Vect}_R is R-linear and exact, sending \mathbf{1} to R and the Frobenius pairing on A to a non-degenerate R-bilinear form on \tau(A). At each finite level, the unit–counit trace \mathrm{tr}_n(\alpha) = (\varepsilon \circ \alpha \circ \eta)(\mathbf{1}), where \eta and \varepsilon are the unit and counit of the Hopf structure on A_n, is G_q-invariant by naturality (they are morphisms in \mathbf{C}, hence invariant under monoidal automorphisms of \tau). The descent homomorphisms \mathfrak{d}_n (descent) are equivariant and satisfy \mathrm{tr}_n \circ \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} = \mathrm{tr}_{n+1}, so by the universal property of the direct limit, the system \{\mathrm{tr}_n\} determines a G_q-invariant R-linear functional \varphi \colon \mathcal{A}_\infty \to R.

Uniqueness. The vanishing condition \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 of the quantum observable universe axioms implies, via Schur's lemma, that \mathrm{End}_{G_q}(\mathbf{1}) \cong R. A G_q-invariant functional \psi \colon \mathcal{A}_\infty \to R must factor through the G_q-fixed subalgebra \mathcal{A}_\infty^{G_q}, and the vanishing condition forces this fixed subalgebra to be one-dimensional (any non-scalar G_q-invariant endomorphism would yield a non-zero element of \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A))). Hence \psi is determined up to scalar by its value on the identity, and normalising \psi(\mathrm{id}) = 1 gives \psi = \varphi. \square
ex:vacuum-state-su2:
Example Constructive vacuum state: the q-Haar integral on \mathrm{SU}_q(2). One explicitly constructs the vacuum state \varphi for the direct limit algebra of \mathrm{SU}(2). One replaces the abstract direct-limit existence argument with a closed-form formula.

Step 1: the Frobenius trace at finite level. At level n of the brane tower, the endomorphism algebra \mathrm{End}(A_n) carries the Frobenius trace:

  \mathrm{tr}_n(\alpha)
  = (\varepsilon \circ \alpha \circ \eta)(\mathbf{1}),

where \eta \colon \mathbb{C} \to A_n is the unit and \varepsilon \colon A_n \to \mathbb{C} is the counit. For A_n = \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) with its Peter–Weyl decomposition, this evaluates to:

  \mathrm{tr}_n(f)
  = \sum_{j=0}^{n} (2j+1) \int_{\mathrm{SU}(2)}
    f(g)\,\overline{\chi_j(g)}\,dg
  \cdot \delta_{j,0}
  = \int_{\mathrm{SU}(2)} f(g)\,dg.

The map \mathrm{tr}_n is the Haar integral restricted to representations of spin \leq n.

Step 2: the q-deformed Haar integral. In the quantum group \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2)), the Haar state \varphi is the unique \mathrm{SU}_q(2)-invariant linear functional normalised by \varphi(1) = 1. Its action on the matrix coefficients t^j_{m,m'} is:

  \varphi(t^j_{m,m'}) = \delta_{j,0}\,\delta_{m,0}\,\delta_{m',0}.

On products, one computes the Haar state via the Woronowicz--Peter--Weyl orthogonality:

  \varphi\bigl((t^j_{m,n})^* \cdot t^{j'}_{m',n'}\bigr)
  = \frac{\delta_{jj'}\,\delta_{mm'}\,\delta_{nn'}}{[2j+1]_q},

where [k]_q = (q^k - q^{-k})/(q - q^{-1}) is the quantum integer.

Step 3: uniqueness verification. Any G_q-invariant functional \psi satisfies \psi \circ \mathrm{Ad}(g) = \psi for all g \in G_q. By the quantum Schur lemma, \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 (the adjoint V_1 contains no trivial summand). The G_q-fixed subalgebra of \mathcal{A}_\infty is \mathbb{C}. Normalising \psi(1) = 1 forces \psi = \varphi. \square

Convergence rate. The Frobenius traces \mathrm{tr}_n converge to \varphi exponentially. For f \in A_n with spin content \leq J:

  |\mathrm{tr}_n(f) - \varphi(f)| = 0
  \quad\text{for all } n \geq J.

The convergence is exact after finitely many steps. The discrete Peter–Weyl decomposition eliminates the need for an \epsilon-\delta argument.

Bring's surface specialisation. On Bring's QOU at the specific aether parameter q_0 (recorded in the archimedean witness ledger), the Haar state evaluates to:

  \varphi(t^j_{m,m'})
  = \frac{\delta_{j,0}\,\delta_{m,0}\,\delta_{m',0}}{1},
  \qquad
  [2j+1]_{q_0}
  = \frac{q_0^{2j+1} - q_0^{-(2j+1)}}{q_0 - q_0^{-1}}.

For j = \frac{1}{2}, one has [2]_{q_0} = q_0 + q_0^{-1} \approx 2.011. For j = 1, one has [3]_{q_0} = q_0^2 + 1 + q_0^{-2} \approx 3.044. These quantum dimensions determine the normalisation of the vacuum state at each spin level.
prop:global-gluing: Proposition Global gluing via twisted quantization. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with aether parameter q. The local deformations of the Frobenius–Hopf object A induce a twisted associative deformation admitting a unique global gluing via Yekutieli's twisted quantization map [yekutieli2008, yekutieli2010]: the direct limit algebra \mathcal{A}_\infty (direct limit algebra) is a well-defined global section of a sheaf of twisted deformation algebras on the underlying site \mathcal{S}.
prf:global-gluing:
Proof Proof of global gluing via twisted quantization. At each point p \in M, the fibre algebra \mathcal{O}_{q(p)}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) is a pronilpotent deformation of \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) in the formal parameter \hbar_q(p) = 1 - q(p)^{-1} (quantum planck constant). According to [yekutieli2008], the coordinate bundle \mathrm{Coor}_M of M (the bundle of formal coordinate systems) carries a twisted deformation datum: a connection and a Maurer–Cartan element in a pronilpotent DG Lie algebra [yekutieli2009]. The obstruction classes \kappa_n (quantum characteristic classes) control whether these local twisted deformations glue across coordinate patches.

The vanishing condition \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 (quantum observable universe) ensures the gerbe \mathfrak{G}_n of local lifts has trivial band at the level of isomorphisms. Consequently, by Theorem 0.10.1 of [yekutieli2015-twisted-dq], the twisted deformations at each fibre patch together into a global sheaf of algebras on M. The direct limit \mathcal{A}_\infty = \varinjlim\Gamma(J^1 \mathcal{S}_n, \mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2)) comprises the global sections of this sheaf, and the vacuum state \tau (vacuum state) extends uniquely via the \mathrm{SU}(2)-averaging argument of that proposition.
rem:global-gluing-interpretation: Remark Global vacuum state and archimedean realisation. The vacuum state is well-defined globally despite local non-commutativity. In the archimedean realisation, this manifests as the global gluing of the local algebras \mathcal{O}_{q(p)}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) over the manifold M.
prop:ordering-jet-compatibility:
Proposition The admissible ordering extends through the jet tower. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with braiding-induced ordering \prec_c on the Hecke basis of A (temporal braiding, axiom 5). Let A_0 = A \hookrightarrow A_1 \hookrightarrow A_2 \hookrightarrow \cdots be the recursive brane tower (recursive brane tower), with A_{n+1} = J^1(A_n) (jet prolongation). One has:

  1. (Extension.) At each level n, the jet prolongation \ell_n \colon A_n \hookrightarrow A_{n+1} induces an admissible ordering \prec_{n+1} on the Hecke basis of A_{n+1} that extends \prec_n:
  a \prec_n b \implies \ell_n(a) \prec_{n+1} \ell_n(b), \qquad a, b \in A_n.

  1. (Compatibility with multiplication.) The ordering \prec_{n+1} satisfies left and right compatibility. If a \prec_{n+1} b, then c \cdot a \prec_{n+1} c \cdot b and a \cdot d \prec_{n+1} b \cdot d for all c, d \in A_{n+1} (admissible system).

  2. (Well-foundedness.) Each \prec_n is well-founded. There are no infinite descending chains in the Hecke basis of A_n.

  3. (Direct limit.) The direct limit algebra \mathcal{A}_\infty = \varinjlim \mathrm{End}(A_n) (direct limit algebra) carries a filtered admissible ordering \prec_\infty = \bigcup_n \prec_n. Every element a \in \mathcal{A}_\infty has a well-defined leading monomial \mathrm{LM}(a) with respect to \prec_\infty. The Gröbner--Shirshov reduction algorithm terminates on every element of \mathcal{A}_\infty that belongs to a finite level A_n.
prf:ordering-jet-compatibility:
Proof Proof of ordering jet compatibility. (1) Extension. At level n, the Hecke basis of A_n is a monomial basis B_n in the generators \sigma_1^{(n)}, \ldots, \sigma_{d_n - 1}^{(n)}. The jet prolongation A_{n+1} = A_n \otimes \Omega^1(A_n) introduces \dim(\Omega^1) = 3 new directions (in the \mathrm{SU}(2) case: \omega_1, \omega_2, \omega_3). Define \prec_{n+1} by degree-lexicographic extension: monomials in B_n keep their relative order; new generators \omega_i are ordered after all level-n generators. This preserves the ordering on the image of \ell_n and well-orders the new monomials.

(2) Compatibility. The Frobenius–Hopf structure on A_{n+1} is inherited from A_n by jet prolongation (jet prolongation). The comultiplication \Delta_{n+1} and multiplication \mu_{n+1} satisfy the same Hecke relation T^2 = (q - q^{-1})T + 1 at level n+1. Degree-lexicographic orderings are compatible with any associative multiplication whose defining relations have leading terms of bounded degree — the Hecke relation is quadratic, so this holds.

(3) Well-foundedness. The degree-lexicographic ordering on B_{n+1} is well-ordered because: (a) total degree is bounded below by 0; (b) at fixed degree, lexicographic ordering on a finite alphabet is well-ordered. The finiteness of the alphabet at each level is guaranteed by the Frobenius–Hopf axioms (the algebra is finitely generated at each level).

(4) Direct limit. For any a \in \mathcal{A}_\infty, there exists n such that a \in \mathrm{End}(A_n). The leading monomial \mathrm{LM}(a) is computed in B_n with respect to \prec_n. By (1), \mathrm{LM}(a) is the same whether computed in B_n or in B_m for any m \geq n — the embedding \ell_n preserves leading monomials. The Gröbner--Shirshov reduction algorithm applied to a in A_n terminates by (3); the same reduction is valid in \mathcal{A}_\infty. \square

Consequence for time. The braiding-induced ordering \prec_c on A_0 propagates through the entire jet tower. At every brane level, "forward time" (Gröbner--Shirshov reduction, braiding) and "backward time" (anti-involution, unbraiding) are well-defined and compatible with the algebraic structure. The arrow of time is inherited from the initial ordering; it does not need to be re-imposed at each level.
sec:mass-brane-intro:
The direct-limit algebra provides the arena for a categorical notion of mass. One defines mass as a Frobenius trace. One shows it is well-defined and unique. One connects it to the obstruction class through Euler-characteristic stability.

One establishes that mass arises as a non-commutativity invariant of the direct-limit algebra. One proves that the categorical Euler characteristic \chi(A_n) is constant along the tower. This supplies the topological invariant for the mass identity. One constructs the mass as a categorical trace. One verifies this trace passes through the brane tower and is the unique compatible Frobenius pairing. One conjectures the specific form of homological shell condensation: the BB-stratified E_\infty^{p,>0}(n) = 0 at the magic values of n.

The next section, Betti Numbers and Harmonic Basis, uses the Euler-characteristic stability and categorical mass to refine the theory with Hodge-theoretic data.
prop:euler-char-stability:
Proposition Stability of the categorical trace and of the base Euler characteristic. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with archimedean realisation over the base curve M_0, and let \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0} be its recursive brane tower. Two quantities are stable under jet prolongation, and they are different quantities.

  1. The categorical trace. \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_{A_{n+1}}) = \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_{A_n}) in \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}) \cong R: prolongation preserves the rigidity data of A_n, hence its quantum dimension.
  2. The Euler characteristic of the base. \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) is unchanged, because prolongation alters the bundle data over M_0 and never M_0 itself.

The Euler characteristic of the total space \mathcal{S}_n is not stable: for the projectivised frame bundle S^2 \hookrightarrow \mathcal{S}_{n+1} \to \mathcal{S}_n, multiplicativity gives \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}_{n+1}) = 2\,\chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(\mathcal{S}_n).
prf:euler-char-stability:
Proof Proof of Stability of the Euler characteristic. Part (1). The categorical trace \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_{A_n}) = \mathrm{ev}_n \circ \mathrm{coev}_n is the rigidity trace of the identity, the composition \mathbf{1} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{coev}_n} A_n \otimes A_n^{\vee} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{ev}_n} \mathbf{1}; in a pivotal category this is the quantum dimension \dim_q(A_n).

Jet prolongation is a functor on \mathbf{C} that preserves the Frobenius–Hopf structure (jet prolongation): the prolonged object A_{n+1} inherits its rigidity data from A_n. Specifically, the unit \eta_{n+1} and counit \varepsilon_{n+1} of A_{n+1} are the images of \eta_n and \varepsilon_n under the prolongation functor, and likewise for the evaluation and coevaluation morphisms: \mathrm{ev}_{n+1} = \mathrm{ev}_n and \mathrm{coev}_{n+1} = \mathrm{coev}_n as elements of \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathbf{1}) \cong R.

Therefore

  \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_{A_{n+1}})
  =
  \mathrm{ev}_{n+1} \circ \mathrm{coev}_{n+1}
  =
  \mathrm{ev}_n \circ \mathrm{coev}_n
  =
  \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_{A_n}),

and by induction \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_{A_n}) = \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_{A_0}) for all n \geq 0. The vanishing condition \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 ensures that the prolongation functor cannot introduce non-trivial twisting of the trace: there are no non-scalar G_q-invariant endomorphisms that could modify the rigidity pairing at each level. This proves the stability of the categorical trace; it says nothing about the base. \square
sec:betti-harmonic-intro:
The Euler characteristic stabilizes along the tower, aggregating Hodge-theoretic data. One now refines this aggregate into Betti numbers, fixes a q-harmonic basis, and filters the basis into fermionic and bosonic sectors via the curvature commutator.

The Betti numbers of the brane tower track the dimensions b_k(A_n) packaged by the Euler characteristic. The q-harmonic basis chooses representatives compatible with the aether parameter, splitting by \mathrm{SU}(2) weight. The algebraic filter [\text{--}, F] then classifies this basis into commuting (bosonic) and anti-commuting (fermionic) sectors. The distributional connection at the limit prepares the geometry for descent.

The next section projects the brane tower onto its physically realised stratum using this fermion--boson filter and eigenspace data.
rem:betti-numbers-brane: Remark Betti numbers of the brane tower. Let b_k(\mathcal{S}_n) = \dim H^k(\mathcal{S}_n, \mathbb{R}) denote the k-th Betti number of \mathcal{S}_n. Since \mathcal{S}_{n+1} is the bundle of orthonormal frames of J^1 \mathcal{S}_n, the Leray--Serre spectral sequence of the fibration \mathcal{S}_{n+1} \to \mathcal{S}_n determines the Betti numbers of \mathcal{S}_{n+1}. The quantum characteristic classes obstruct the collapse of this spectral sequence, controlling the growth of b_k(\mathcal{S}_{n+1}) relative to b_k(\mathcal{S}_n).
rem:q-harmonic-basis-brane:
Remark q-Harmonic basis of the brane tower. For each level n, the q-harmonic 1-forms \alpha_{n,i} belong to the space \mathcal{H}^1(\mathcal{S}_n, \mathrm{ad} \mathcal{S}_n) of harmonic 1-forms on \mathcal{S}_n with values in the adjoint bundle \mathrm{ad} \mathcal{S}_n. They are characterised by the self-duality condition relative to the instanton connection A_n (recursive brane tower):

  \alpha_{n,i} \in \mathcal{H}^1
  \iff
  d_{A_n}\alpha = 0
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  d_{A_n}^*\alpha = 0.

The Hodge-star operator is induced by the Hermitian metric that the Levi form L (aether parameter) defines on the horizontal distribution. The index i runs over 1 \leq i \leq b_1(\mathcal{S}_n) (Betti numbers on branes).

At the base level n = 0 the index range above gives b_1(\mathcal{S}_0) = 3, hence three primary basis vectors \{\phi_1, \phi_2, \phi_3\}. At level n = 1 the basis lifts: it includes the original modes together with their J^1 prolongations (jet prolongation), which act as the first-order resolutions of the base flows.
rem:weight-space-decomposition:
Remark Weight-space decomposition of the harmonic basis. The adjoint bundle \mathrm{ad} \mathcal{S}_n has fibre \mathfrak{su}(2). Via the weight-space decomposition of \mathrm{SU}(2), the harmonic basis of \mathcal{H}^1(\mathcal{S}_n, \mathrm{ad} \mathcal{S}_n) splits into two families.

Longitudinal modes. These forms constitute the \mathrm{U}(1) backbone. They take values in the Cartan subalgebra of \mathfrak{su}(2) and have the geometric form \vartheta^0 \otimes H, where H is the diagonal generator. They represent steady-state laminar flows aligned with the \mathrm{U}(1) subgroup. If the bundle splits at a monodromy fixed point, these are the only modes that survive; they correspond to the magnetic flux of the stable vortices.

Ladder modes. These are the raising and lowering vortices. They take values in the off-diagonal generators E_\pm of \mathfrak{su}(2) and have the geometric form \vartheta^\pm \otimes E_\pm. They describe entangling flows that twist the \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) fibre along the brane. These modes generate the non-commutativity in the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) algebra (direct limit algebra).

In the 1-jet bundle J^1 \mathcal{S}_n (J^1\mathcal{S} local states), each basis element \alpha is a pair consisting of a value (the direction of the \mathrm{SU}(2) flow in the fibre) and a momentum (the gradient of that flow relative to the complex structure of the brane).
prop:algebraic-filter-classification:
Proposition Fermion--boson classification by commutator with curvature. Let F_A be the curvature of the aether parameter (aether parameter) and let \alpha be a harmonic 1-form in the q-harmonic basis on branes (q-harmonic basis).

The commutator [F_A, \alpha] classifies \alpha into exactly one of two types:

  1. Fermionic (matter). [F_A, \alpha] \neq 0.
  2. Bosonic (radiation). [F_A, \alpha] = 0.
rem:algebraic-filter-physical:
Remark Physical reading of the fermion/boson filter. The two commutator classes of the fermion--boson filter carry a geometric reading in the gauge-fluid flow.

  1. Fermionic (matter). When [F_A, \alpha] \neq 0, the form \alpha is entangled with the curvature. It sees the \mathrm{SO}(3) holonomy and the index -6 fixed points, yielding geodesics that are trapped or spiralling around the fundamental vortex filaments.
  2. Bosonic (radiation). When [F_A, \alpha] = 0, the form \alpha commutes with the curvature. It corresponds to longitudinal modes that propagate through the bulk without deflection by the monodromy fixed points, yielding straight geodesics relative to the gauge-fluid flow.
rem:algebraic-filter:
Remark The algebraic filter. Let \alpha be a harmonic 1-form in the basis of q-harmonic basis on branes. Its signature is determined by its commutator with the curvature F_A (aether parameter).

  1. Fermionic type (matter). [F_A, \alpha] \neq 0. These forms are entangled with the curvature. They see the \mathrm{SO}(3) holonomy and the index -6 fixed points, yielding geodesics trapped or spiralling around the three fundamental vortex filaments.
  2. Bosonic type (radiation). [F_A, \alpha] = 0. These forms commute with the curvature. As longitudinal modes (weight space decomposition), they flow through the bulk undeflected by monodromy fixed points, yielding straight geodesics relative to the gauge-fluid flow.
